title: Compact Connectivity Impact Strip and Eviction-safe Upgrade Flow
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem:
Currently our private console upgrade flow is optimistic about cluster-wide evictions and surfaces a long table of affected tenant subnets. Operators need a compact, scannable view that highlights connectivity and SLO risk at-a-glance and then lets them step into remediation/rollback actions without context switching.

Goal:
Design a compact "connectivity impact strip" — a horizontal, per-cluster summary bar that encodes connectivity risk, expected eviction surface, and SLO exposure for the selected upgrade window. Pair that with an "eviction-safe upgrade" flow that recommends non-disruptive rollout batches and exposes quick mitigations (circuit-breaker toggle, region shielding, traffic fence) inline.

Scope / Out of scope:
- In scope: Private Console UX for cluster upgrade workflow, connectivity strip component, rollout batch recommendations, inline mitigations, prototype for usability testing.
- Out of scope: backend rollout engine changes, autoscaling policies, billing changes.

Personas:
- Cluster Operator (primary): wants a one-line summary showing whether an upgrade will cause tenant disruptions and which mitigations to apply.
- Platform PM / SRE (secondary): wants to audit decisions and have links to telemetry.

User journeys:
1) Operator lands on cluster > Upgrades. Top of page shows the Connectivity Impact Strip summarizing the selected upgrade plan.
2) Operator hovers a risky segment to see quick modal: affected subnets, tenants count, expected eviction probability, SLO exposure (p99 latency increase risk).
3) Operator clicks "Generate eviction-safe plan" to receive suggested batches with a confidence score and recommended mitigations.
4) Operator applies plan and can optionally toggle an automated rollback guard.

Design constraints and principles:
- Compactness: primary strip must fit within a single row without wrapping on typical 1200px canvas.
- Scanability: color legend, micro-annotations, and keyboard focus states.
- Explainability: each encoded metric must be explorable with a single click.
- Accessibility: ensure color contrast and provide text fallback in compressed mode.

Acceptance criteria:
- Visual spec and interactive Figma prototype produced covering default, compressed, and keyboard-only modes.
- Usability test (5 operators) shows median time-to-decision under 90s for a sample upgrade scenario.
- Design handoff artifacts (tokens, spacing, component props) in the repo and PR (see attachments).

Notes on data mapping and backend hooks:
- Strip segments map to the platform's pre-existing "egress-path" telemetry ID and SLO exposure metric. When unavailable, show "unknown" with a recommended preflight check.
- Confidence scores are computed by backend; design will show rounded scores and explainers.

Deliverables:
- Figma prototype (interactive) of the strip + hover modal + batch suggestion panel.
- Design tokens and component spec for React.
- Usability test script and summary.
- Review doc summarizing accessibility checks and edge cases.
decisions: Use a horizontal strip with segmented chips (not a stacked list) to maximize scanability.
Encode risk with three tiers: Low / Medium / High plus an 'Unknown' state when telemetry is missing.
Batch recommendation CTA will open a preview panel; applying the plan requires a two-step confirm with optional rollback guard.
Compressed mode will replace colored chips with text tag and sentinel icon for accessibility and narrow screens.
open_questions: Should confidence score be shown as percentage or 0-10? (backend prefers percentage)
What SLO exposure threshold counts as 'High' — product wants p99 > 20% increase, SRE suggests 10%.
How should multi-cluster upgrades be represented if the plan spans >1 cluster? (current design is cluster-scoped)
Do we need a separate audit event for using 'Generate eviction-safe plan' to satisfy compliance?
